summary: Miqyas logged 62 articles in this seven-day window, and the political column carried the heaviest negative tilt. Ten stories (16.1%) were rated politically negative against just three (4.8%) rated positive, a gap wider than in either of the other categories. The ten politically negative stories line up exactly with the ten articles the crawl flagged for review this week, so the flags were not scattered noise: they tracked one cluster of domestic political disputes, ranging from a NAB inquiry involving the son of JUI-F chief Fazlur Rehman to the Election Commission suspending the Islamabad local government poll schedule after a court stay.

The dominant storyline was a widening public dispute within and around the governing coalition. It began with a Dawn report, based on unnamed official sources, that President Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif agreed any referendum on new provinces would need parliamentary approval. PPP chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari then condemned what a PPP statement called government action against JUI-F, and followed with a Karachi speech in which he said the system was 'made to collapse' and called for a political reset. Federal ministers Khawaja Asif and Attaullah Tarar answered by questioning the PPP's record and backing a referendum. By the end of the week JUI-F said security for Fazlur Rehman and his family had been withdrawn, which an Islamabad police official described as involving only one guard. Miqyas takes no position on any of these claims; each is attributed to the party that made it.

Social coverage had the largest raw negative share, at 19.4% (12 stories), yet its causes were mostly physical and civic hazards rather than political argument: hazardous smog readings in Lahore and wider Punjab, an NDMA high alert for severe dry conditions in four Sindh districts, a UN agency finding that Punjab's water demand exceeds supply, militant attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and the death of a 13-year-old domestic worker in Islamabad. Economic coverage was the calmest of the three, at 74.2% neutral, with nine positive readings (14.5%) tied to items such as a $500m ADB loan for pension reform, a World Bank 'satisfactory' rating on a health programme, and a Saudi framework deal to study roughly $30bn of energy investment. Its seven negatives leaned toward climate and supply risk, plus a Punjab sugar standoff in which mills ignored a government order to begin crushing.

Despite how charged the coalition dispute was, the lean readings stayed almost entirely balanced: 60 of 62 stories were rated balanced and two pro-government, with none pro-opposition. One of the two was the Dawn report built around ministers' rebuttals of Bilawal with no PPP reply included. AI confidence leaned toward the middle, with 34 medium ratings against 28 high and no low ratings. The medium calls clustered on the political stories: eight of the ten flagged articles were rated medium, mostly because they rested on one party's statement, anonymous sources, or disputed accounts, such as the conflicting party and police versions of the Fazlur Rehman security withdrawal. Readers should treat those stories as claims still awaiting a full public record.

notableStories.headline: In hard-hitting speech, Bilawal says system was 'made to collapse'
notableStories.context: Bilawal Bhutto Zardari's Karachi speech calling for a political reset, including talks with PTI, set the tone for the week's coalition dispute.

notableStories.headline: 'He who claims equity must come with clean hands': Asif hits back at Bilawal
notableStories.context: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif's rebuttal to Bilawal, backing a referendum on new provinces, showed the dispute had become an open exchange between coalition partners.

notableStories.headline: Security withdrawn from Fazl, family members
notableStories.context: JUI-F said security for Fazlur Rehman and his family was withdrawn, while police said only one guard was affected, marking a sharp escalation in the government's standoff with JUI-F.

notableStories.headline: Punjab sugar millers snub order to begin crushing from weekend
notableStories.context: Punjab's sugar mills largely ignored a provincial deadline to start crushing, leaving growers demanding a support price and raising questions about enforcement.

notableStories.headline: ECP suspends Islamabad LG polls programme
notableStories.context: The Election Commission suspended Islamabad's December 20 local government poll schedule after a court stay, extending a long delay in local elections for the capital.
